issue_context.title: test/e2e: use framework helpers to create namespaces
issue_context.body:
### What would you like to be added?

Currently, some e2e tests do not use central framework helper methods to create namespaces. Examples:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/296bf4f01668374ade252a751d4c3567917b9890/test/e2e/apimachinery/webhook.go#L1532
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/296bf4f01668374ade252a751d4c3567917b9890/test/e2e/apimachinery/webhook.go#L2370-L2375
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/296bf4f01668374ade252a751d4c3567917b9890/test/e2e/network/netpol/kubemanager.go#L178

The fix is to use https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/296bf4f01668374ade252a751d4c3567917b9890/test/e2e/framework/framework.go#L519 instead.

### Why is this needed?

This makes maintanance of e2e tests hard as enforcement settings (like pod security admission) is not centralized

I'm running into an issue because of this. When running netpol e2e tests on GKE, the tests actually fail because the default ServiceAccount for the test namespaces take too long to be created, and unlike the framework helpers, the netpol-specific helpers for Namespace creation do NOT wait for ServiceAccount creation. After creating the Namespace, the netpol tests immediately try to create Pods in the Namespace, which fail as the ServiceAccount does not exist yet. We only observe this issue on GKE clusters, but this is not specific to GKE in itself.

See https://github.com/antrea-io/antrea/issues/3762
We've run into this issue as well in OCP see https://github.com/openshift/origin/pull/26775

@astoycos I already have a PR for this: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/111789. It's pretty comprehensive, as when I started working on this, I realized there were several things that needed fixing in the netpol tests.
